title: Fix 'Could not open lock file' when apt runs without sudo
summary: apt installs software for the whole system, so only the administrator (root) may change its database. Running apt as a normal user gives 'Could not open lock file' with 'Permission denied'. Run the same command with sudo.
error_patterns: Unable to acquire the dpkg frontend lock

aliases.text: unable to acquire the dpkg frontend lock
why apt install says permission denied
apt отказано в доступе при установке
не могу установить пакет apt нет прав

prerequisites: An account that is allowed to use sudo (you know its password).

steps.explain: Check which user the terminal runs as. The error appears when apt runs as a normal user, because only root may write to the apt lock file. The output should be your login name, not root.
steps.expect: Prints your login name, for example alex. If it prints root, the error has another cause; compare the full message.

steps.explain: Check that your account may use sudo. sudo asks for your password and changes nothing else.
steps.expect: Asks for your password and returns to the prompt. If it says 'may not run sudo', this account cannot install software; ask the computer's administrator.

steps.explain: Run the same install command with sudo. sudo asks for your password once (nothing is shown while you type), then apt runs as administrator. Answer y when apt asks 'Do you want to continue?'.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: Name of the program or library to install.

steps.expect: apt reads the package lists, shows the packages to install, and ends with 'Setting up <PACKAGE>'. The 'Permission denied' lines do not appear.

alternatives.explain: The same install done with apt-get, the older apt tool. Use it if apt keeps printing its unstable-interface warning or your guide uses apt-get.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: Name of the program or library to install.

alternatives.expect: Lists the packages and installs them, or prints 'is already the newest version' if it is already installed.

verify.expect: Shows 'Status: install ok installed' for the package.

rollback.explain: Remove the package again if you installed the wrong one. Your other programs are kept.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: Name of the package to remove.

warnings: Installing with sudo runs the package's install scripts as administrator. Install only software you know and trust.
Do not delete /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend or other lock files to get around this error. They protect the package database from damage.
If the message says 'held by process' instead, another package manager (for example the Software Updater) is still running. Wait for it to finish, then try again.
